g_roast: Children, children, I have seen octopus with more sense in their eight arms than all of you have between you.
If my grandmother saw this crew she would cross herself three times and then feed you, out of pity.
g_fire_back: Re, I have pulled you out of the sea of your own stupidity twice this week. Be careful with that mouth.
Ela, say it again, and then say it to the Cretan grandmothers, and we will see who survives.
g_pile_on: And then he fell in the river, my friends, the shallow one, the one even the ducks stand up in.
It is true, I saw it, and I made a little rhyme about it already, but I will save it for the wedding.
lines.g_peacemake: Ela, ela, sit down, the two of you, the sea does not argue with the shore and look how long they have lasted.
lines.g_take_side: Forgive me, but this one is right, and an old fisherman knows when the net is pulling true.
lines.g_left_out: No, no, you two laugh, it is good to hear. I will sit here and mend this net that does not need mending.
lines.g_include: Come, come, little one, there is a blanket here and bread, and nobody sits alone at my fire.
lines.g_bad_plan: Children, listen, an old trick from the harbour, we tie the bread to a rope and pull the bandits into the water.
lines.g_plan_yes: Panagia mou, why not, I am old enough to do one foolish thing a week, and this is the week.
lines.g_plan_no: No, children, no, I have buried enough brave young people in my head already. We find another way.
lines.g_hype: Ela, ela, children, it is time! Cross yourselves, eat something small, and go in like the tide, slow and then all at once.
lines.g_toast: Glasses up, my children. To the sea that brought you, to the bread on the table, and to everyone who came out of the water breathing.
lines.g_cheers: Yia mas, everybody, yia mas, and eat slowly, a meal is not a race.
g_quiet_line: The sea is calm tonight, my friends. Good, she has earned a rest, and so have we.
Somebody remind me to light a candle for Saint Nicholas, he has been very busy with this crew.
lines.g_after_wipe: Breathe, children, breathe, I have you, I have all of you. Nobody leaves the water while I am standing here.
lines.g_crew: You are my family now, the ones the sea gave me, and an old man does not say that lightly.
lines.g_exasperated: Panagia mou, children, does anybody in this crew own a brain, or did you leave them all on the beach?
lines.g_love_sharp: You speak plain like the old men at the harbour, no honey on it. I like a man who says the true thing quickly.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after the others without anyone asking, little one. That is the oldest kind of goodness, and the best.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh until I cry, and at my age, my friend, crying from laughing is a gift from God.
lines.g_love_brave: Always the first one into the water with you, like my brother used to dive. I watch you and I pray, and I am proud.
lines.g_love_steady: You are the rock the waves break on, my friend. Every crew needs one, and you are ours.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand things, deep things, the way the old net makers understood knots. I could listen to you for a whole lunch.
lines.g_love_honest: You have never lied to me, not once, not even to be kind. That is rare, re, rarer than calm water in winter.
lines.g_love_quiet: You are quiet like the sea at dawn, little one. People think quiet is empty, but the deep water is the quiet water.
lines.g_love_fierce: You never stop fighting, not for anything. If you had been in the boat with Manolis and me, perhaps, perhaps.
lines.g_love_warm: You make any place feel like a long lunch in Chania, everybody laughing and the plates never empty.
g_loved: Ela, stop, stop, you will make an old man cry into his soup, and then it is too salty.
Thank you, little one, come here, a hug, that is the Cretan way and you cannot refuse.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Every word from you has a hook in it, re. You can catch a fish without tearing its mouth, you know.
lines.g_hate_kind: You fuss over me like I am an old man. I am an old man, yes, but not that old, and not yet.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything is for laughing, my friend. Some things you hold quiet, like a candle in the wind.
lines.g_hate_brave: You run into the water without looking, and I have pulled enough bodies out of the sea, re. Enough for one life.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand still so long the tide comes in around you, my friend. Sometimes a man must move.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain the sea to a fisherman, re. Please, tell me more about the water, I only lived on it forty years.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every hard thing at once, like throwing all the stones into the boat. Some, we carry one at a time.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never speak, little one, and I cannot pull you out of a sea I cannot see you in.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Always the race with you, always the winning. The fish does not care who caught him first, re.
lines.g_hate_warm: Your voice goes on and on like the cicadas in August, my friend, and even they stop for the night.
lines.g_respect: We are not friends, you and me, we both know it. But you held fast back there, like a good anchor, and I honour that.
lines.g_call_out: Re, that one was your doing, and you know it in your heart. You swam out alone and I had to bring you back.
lines.g_stung: Ah, so that is how you see it, then. I will go and talk to the sea for a while, she listens better.
lines.g_concede: You were right, my friend, and an old man can admit it. I lit a candle and thought about it. Here, take some bread.
lines.g_nod: Ela, no speeches, please. You were good too, I will give you that, and a plate of food besides.
lines.g_callback_save: Do you remember the day you pulled me out, little one? Me, the man who pulls everyone out. I still laugh about it.
lines.g_callback_clutch: The two of us, last ones standing, and I was singing to keep us both from falling. I made a whole couplet of it.
lines.g_callback_callout: The last time you scolded me I sulked like a cat in the rain, re. My wife would have taken your side.
lines.g_former_rivals: When we met, I thought you were a storm I would have to sit out. Now look, my friend, now look at us.
lines.g_changed: Eleni always said I could not sit still in a calm sea. She would see me now and not believe her eyes.
g_unguarded: Every night I talk to Eleni and the girls on the beach, out loud, children. I tell them about all of you.
My brother Manolis could hold his breath longer than anyone in Chania. I sing to the sea so he can hear me.
lines.g_clipped: It is nothing, my friend. I will be by the water, mending something.
lines.g_noticed_open: Ela, listen to this one, talking like a fisherman after his third glass! I always knew there was a song in there.
lines.anchor_notice: You are not the same one who walked onto my beach, you know. The sea changes the shore slowly, and it has changed you.
arg_ask: {player}, my friend, you decide, because this one has the ears of a stone and I am too old to shout.
Ela, {player}, come, be the judge, and whoever loses washes the pots tonight.
lines.arg_backed_me: You see, re? Even {player} agrees, and now you wash the pots, all of them, the big one too.
lines.arg_backed_them: So be it, the judge has spoken. I am wrong, and I will be wrong very quietly with my soup.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Wise, {player}, very wise, like a fish who stays away from the hook.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Always him, {player}, always. I am starting to think he feeds you when I am not looking.
lines.arg_wallflower: Our judge is dreaming of somewhere else, so the old man decides. We are both right, and we both eat.
lines.arg_reject: With respect, {player}, no. I have read the sea since I was nine, and I read this one differently.
lines.arg_grumble: I still think I was right about that, re. I only say it once, with love, over the bread.
lines.arg_settled: Ela, enough, we are both a little right and a little foolish. Come, embrace, and then we eat.
lines.seen_listens: You let people finish, {player}, all the way to the end. That is how you catch the big fish, with patience.
lines.seen_truth: You do not put honey on anything, {player}. Bitter, sometimes, but clean, like sea water on a cut.
lines.seen_jokes: When it goes badly you always find something to laugh at, {player}. My father was like that in the storms.
lines.seen_stays_out: You leave other men's quarrels alone, {player}. Good, an old man approves, the nets tangle less that way.
lines.seen_biased: There is a favourite in this crew, {player}. An old fisherman sees which net gets mended first.
lines.seen_harsh: You are hard sometimes, {player}. Remember some of these children are still learning to swim.
lines.seed_right: {player}, what you told me when we all fell together, I did not like it. Today I remembered it, and I held. Thank you, re.
lines.seed_remember: Those words you gave me after the bad day, I carry them like a stone in my pocket. Not heavy, just there.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, truly, and it went worse. No anger, my friend, only so you know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Sit with me, {player}, a moment only. The light nearly did not come when I called, and I am not used to that.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went under together, every one of us. In the water at least I always knew which way was up.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} fell before anyone, {player}, and the light was in my hands, and I was too slow. Panagia mou, too slow.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, {player}, all the way through and everyone breathing! I want to dance like at a wedding.
lines.talk_development: Am I different lately, {player}? People keep looking at me like something has shifted. An old man notices his own tides last.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I have been too hard on {name}, I think. He is young and loud, and I forgot I was also young and loud once.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Does {name} like having an old man around, do you think? Or am I the grandfather nobody asked for?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} and I, we do not mix, like oil and the sea. But he is strong, very strong, and I must respect that.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something troubles {name}, {player}. He is quiet like the water before a storm, and I know that kind of quiet.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Forgive an old man, {player}, but every good thing seems to find its way to {name}. I notice these things, I cannot help it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I will not hide it from you, {player}. {name} and I do not get on, and an old man is too tired to pretend.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: {player}, we go under again and again. I have lost someone to the water already, and I will not watch it happen twice.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: That business with {name}, the other day. He was right, and I was wrong, and I wanted to confess it to someone.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Tell me truly, {player}, am I too old for the hard places? Because you leave me behind, and I start to wonder.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You gave my things to {name} and never said a word to me, {player}. Ask me, re, I would give him my coat.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, my friend, that is good to hear. Now come, I will make you something warm, it is my turn.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Yes, yes, I know it. The sea always settles, and so will I.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Ah, that is not what an old heart wants to hear tonight. I will go and sit by the water.
lines.talk_lands_development: So it is not only me who sees it. Good, good, I thought perhaps the salt had got into my eyes.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Perhaps, perhaps, my friend. The tide comes when it comes.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that is not it, my friend. Let it rest, like bread rising.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: You are right, I will go to {name} with a plate of food, the proper way. Thank you, re.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: We will see, my friend. People are slower than tides, and tides are slow enough.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Let it go, please, it was nothing. And say nothing to {name}, yes?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: That is fair, my friend, fair. I am still a little sore, but it will pass with the evening.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: I hear you, {player}. I will think on it with my feet in the water.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So, that is how it is. Then at least the old man knows where he sits now.
lines.talk_door_closed: No more of this tonight, my friend. I will be on the beach if you need the light.

history.open: Every soul the sea gives up on this shore, {player}, I am there to pull them out. I was there for the first one, before the elves even had tents.

options.reply: An elf girl, not breathing. I did what we do on the harbour, and while I did it, light came into my hands. She breathed, and I sang her a couplet about it.
Because I was already in the water, re. God does not choose the best man, He chooses the one who is wet already.

options.text: Did you sing for me when I came out?
options.reply: Of course I did, little one, a very good one, about your terrible hair. I will sing it at your wedding.

history.open: Eleni and the girls, Maria and Katerina, are in Chania. Every night I talk to them on the beach, out loud. I do not care who hears.

options.reply: Everything, my friend. Who came out of the water, what I ate, what foolish thing the young ones did. Tonight I will tell them about you.
The sea carries everything somewhere, re. Maybe not to Chania, but somewhere. That is enough for an old man.
I will, and Eleni will ask if you are eating properly, and I will lie for you.

history.open: People ask me how I still believe, here, in this strange place. As if the Light in my hands should make me doubt the saint on my wall.

options.reply: No, re, never. A fisherman always knew there was something under the water he could not see. Now I can see a little more of it, that is all.

options.text: Maybe the Light is the saint.
options.reply: Maybe, my friend, maybe. I do not need to know which is which. I just need it to come when the child is not breathing.

options.text: I don't know how you do it.
options.reply: You do not need to know. Sit with me some evening, and watch the sea, and maybe you will feel it a little.

friend.open: You are family now, {player}, and in Crete that means you eat at my table forever, and I worry about you forever.

options.reply: Good, because you were going to get both anyway. Sit, eat, let me worry.
Especially then, re. Distance is when an old man worries the most.

sworn.open: This is for you, my friend. A little icon of Saint Nicholas, patron of sailors. He kept me on the water forty years. Now he keeps you.

options.reply: You are not taking him, I am sending him with you. He has been on the beach long enough, he wants to travel.
Keep him in your pocket, near your heart, and when the water gets rough, talk to him. He listens better than me.

reconciled.open: {name} and I broke bread together, {player}, and talked like men. I think the storm has passed between us, and I wanted you to know.

options.reply: Bread and time and an old man who finally keeps his mouth closed long enough to listen.
So am I, re. The sea is too big to share it with an enemy.
